text:
The Linear workspace this plugin is developed against is the user's REAL working workspace, and another AI agent monitors it.

Never move an issue into the 'Needs Input' or 'QA' workflow states during testing. The other agent watches those states and picks the issue up as work. Test issues may only occupy 'Backlog', 'Done' or 'Canceled'. Leave any issue that is already open alone entirely.

This is not theoretical. During the first round of live testing for create_issue and update_issue, a throwaway test issue triggered the workspace's Symphony automation, which auto-commented on it twice. The user then gave this rule explicitly.

There is no code anchor for this. It constrains how anyone TESTS against the live API, not how the plugin behaves. Prefer mocked tests; the offline suite under tests/ covers the logic without touching the workspace at all.

Also note Linear's delete semantics, learned the hard way during cleanup: issueDelete is a soft delete by default and the issue remains retrievable as trashed, though issueDelete(permanentlyDelete: true) does hard-delete. projectDelete only ever trashes; there is no permanent delete for projects, so test projects linger in the trash for about 30 days.
author: Architect <architect@gnosis>

text: delete_issue is trash-only by the user's decision (2026-09). Rejected alternatives, agreed with the user: (1) an optional permanent/hard-delete flag, rejected because the caller is an LLM that can misread a request and the trash makes mistakes recoverable; add it only if the user asks for a real need. (2) a required confirm parameter, rejected because the LLM fills it as easily as the identifier, so it gives no real protection. Stavrobot has its own confirmation step for destructive tools; the manifest description still says the delete is destructive so the bot asks first.
